title: Memories that fade and sensors that remember
seoTitle: Memories that fade and sensors that remember | Blog, Jorge Parra
description: A photonic chip with fading memory, a simulated phase-change device and a sensor that briefly retains traces of movement.

title: Light learns to travel, remember and change direction
description: A photosynapse retains a trace of light, so the same sensor can respond differently depending on what it has seen before.

title: Light on a chip, ions in a pore and spins in a crystal
description: A symmetric pore lets more ions through in one direction. The explanation lies in the polarisation of the membrane around it.

title: On-demand photons and two ways to test materials with heat
description: Heating a memory device during fabrication can stabilise it. A working perovskite solar cell tells a different story as it heats and cools.

title: Measuring a spectrum, orienting a monolayer and making gold porous
description: Expose two gold films to the same pulse of light and their signals recover at different rates. The one from porous gold takes about three times as long.

title: Lasers, vision and fluctuating memories
description: The fluctuations that complicate reading a memory cell can also tell us about the material that stores the bit. One paper listens to that noise.

title: A two-cycle pulse, a light-sensitive synapse and multilevel memory
description: Thirteen femtoseconds leave room for barely two cycles of the infrared light in the experiment. A lithium niobate waveguide compresses the pulse that far.

title: Sensing heat with light and adjusting current with charge or a field
description: How do you detect absorption by a few molecules? One paper looks for the heat they leave in a waveguide.

title: A gradual image, a delayed neuron and two twisted crystals
description: The junction between two lithium niobate crystals can conduct current. At certain angles between the crystals, the dipoles near the junction rearrange as well.

title: Light between two metals, power on a thin film and a blue diode
description: Apply a volt across a near-atomic gap between a metal tip and a surface, and the light signal at twice the input frequency rises sharply.

title: Networks for light and protons, and an insulator with grain boundaries
description: Grain boundaries are often weak spots in an insulator. A conductive tip scanning an antimony oxide film barely sees a difference between a grain and its boundary.

title: Mixing light and magnetism, storing charge and watching an LED age
description: A perovskite LED runs inside an electron microscope. Watching it under bias lets the researchers pinpoint where degradation begins.

title: Circular light, memory in a synapse and amorphous regions written in a crystal
description: A crystal can remain ordered through most of its volume while losing that order in the regions written into it. One paper looks at how those amorphous regions form.

title: An infrared modulator, a fault-tolerant memory and a ferroelectric solar cell
description: Even with some memristors stuck, an array can still retrieve patterns. The team adapts training to faults measured in the circuit itself.

title: Polarisation in a film, avalanche in a transistor and a transition in VO₂
description: Aligning a ReSe₂ transistor’s channel helps charges multiply at a comparatively low field. A photodetector puts the effect to the test.

title: Computing with light, switching functions with voltage and bending a compound eye
description: How do you assemble a 185-pixel compound eye without breaking the light-sensitive film? The design turns much of the stretching into bending.

title: Continuous terahertz waves, an ionic photosynapse and domain walls
description: Mix two infrared lasers on a very thin surface, and the difference between their frequencies becomes a continuous, tunable terahertz source.

title: Photonics for listening to the spectrum, current for switching a magnet and gold between layers
description: To catch interference as it happens, a photonic chip registers different radio frequencies at different times. The analysis takes less than 110 nanoseconds.

title: Reflecting polaritons, a graphene gate and dipoles that turn
description: In a MoOCl₂ flake, a wave coupled to light travels more than ten micrometres. A microscope follows it as it reflects off the edge.

title: Shrinking a pattern, separating noise and bringing an exciton into view
description: A ferroelectric layer brings an exciton that barely emitted light into view in the spectrum. Twisting the layers changes the strength of the effect.

title: A wireless link, a magnetic junction and photons from an edge
description: At the edge of a perovskite crystal, charges can find their way to a spot that emits photons one at a time.

title: Trimming a finished chip, storing states in a molecule and watching quantum dots
description: A photonic circuit can come out of fabrication slightly off target. One paper looks at how much room there is to tune it afterwards.

title: Growing quantum dots to order, building a neuron and choosing a crystal’s faces
description: A quantum dot at the centre of its resonator releases more usable photons. The team chooses where the dot will grow before building the resonator.

title: Pulses in silicon nitride, stretchable memory and emitters acting together
description: Visible light writes into a flexible transistor, and ultraviolet light helps erase it. The memory still works when the material is stretched in two directions.

title: A liquid-crystal shutter and two ways to use a magnet
description: A quantum dot’s brightness depends on the light reaching it. A voltage across a liquid-crystal film adjusts that illumination while the colour stays the same.

title: Optical cells, deflected currents and light taking a different path
description: A layer just 2.4 nanometres thick behaves differently when another material is placed on top. A sideways current gives clues to what happens at the junction.

title: A flat fibre and two devices for working with images
description: The same film can show a full image or pick out its outlines. The switch comes from changing the electric field that reorients the ferroelectric material.

title: A dispersive lens, a light-sensitive fingerprint and a magnetoelectric oxide
description: Many lenses are designed to keep different colours from straying apart. This week’s metalens puts that separation to work.

title: Polarization, memory and perovskites
description: The same circuit can measure the polarisation of incoming light and prepare the polarisation we want to send. Each task calls for different settings.

title: A waveguide that processes light, flexible transistors and a field-responsive glass
description: A MoS₂ sheet can guide light and also act on the signal it carries. One paper brings both jobs into the same waveguide.

title: Side entry into a waveguide, activity in a neuron and an emitting monolayer
description: Light usually enters a waveguide at one end. Feeding it through the side of a hollow guide changes where the guide can sit in an assembly.

title: Radio beams, microwave computing and plasmons in a crystal
description: A microwave signal changes as it travels through a network. That journey can do some of the computation before the output is read.

title: Reflections for reading a spectrum, motion memory and two responses from one element
description: Reflections inside a waveguide might seem like a nuisance. One paper uses them to tell what spectrum entered the guide.

title: Writing an infrared image, storing charge and thinning silver
description: How does the optical response of silver change as the film grows thinner? The measurements show why thickness matters.

title: A shortcut for light, event-based vision and colour from infrared
description: If part of a scene stays the same, does it need to be recorded again? A transistor array detects changes in light and works from those events.

title: Polaritons along edges, languages in an array and light-activated memory
description: A memristor array helps identify the language of a written text. The paper shows how the task is divided between the algorithm and the operations performed in the circuit.

title: A nonlinear metasurface, high-temperature vision and an adjustable Hall response
description: A junction based on MoS₂ still detects visible light at 450 °C. The study explores what the interface contributes to a sensor that also stores a signal.

title: Carrying high-frequency signals, filtering spikes and forming vortices
description: When a ferroelectric is grown on silicon, its dipoles can arrange themselves into vortices. The puzzle is how those patterns form on a substrate used for circuits.

title: Computing with light, retaining polarisation and turning a mask into an emitter
description: A photonic processor can use power just to hold its settings, even before it computes anything. A ferroelectric modulator can retain a setting on its own.

title: Cavities on a fiber, graphene electrodes and ion channels
description: A small change in a fibre’s radius can trap light in one region. Repeat it and several resonators can sit along the fibre itself.

title: A spin read by light, a magnet that remembers it and a stable dielectric
description: A quantum dot links a hole spin to photons that can travel through fibre. Its dephasing time gives a measure of how long the spin can be manipulated coherently.

title: Light beneath a monolayer, carbon dots and heat in a ferroelectric
description: An insulator can do its electrical job well and still make it harder for heat to escape. One paper examines both demands in the same ferroelectric.

title: Infrared in a suspended guide, a reconfigurable transistor and the first steps of crystal growth
description: To modulate mid-infrared light, a team removes the substrate that would absorb some of it, then designs the suspended guide and its electrodes together.

title: A silicon modulator and two ways to use perovskites
description: A perovskite memory can be written by forming metal filaments or by moving ions within the material. The choice changes the trade-off between retention and endurance.

title: Separating light modes, stabilizing transistors and tracking electrons in graphene
description: Light makes the electrons in graphene oscillate. The experimental challenge is to follow their response within a cycle of the driving wave itself.

title: Moiré light, memory on two timescales and emission from a defect
description: An atomic defect can leave a signature in the light a monolayer emits. The experiment combines the position and colour of the emission to identify it.

title: Light and sound on a chip, stacked transistors and an infrared image
description: An infrared pattern barely shows up until the film that holds it is heated. As the material crystallises, its regions emit different amounts of radiation, revealing the pattern.
